findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows negative slice causing crash or wrong rows
findings.body: File src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 880 does queryset[start_offset:stop] with start_offset = cursor.offset when cursor.offset < 0 and enable_advanced_features is true. Cursor.offset is attacker-controlled via the cursor string (Cursor.from_string parses int(bits[1]) with no validation). Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing and raise AssertionError, turning a crafted cursor into a 500, and the comment claiming Django handles negative slicing automatically is false. Even if it did not raise, Python/DB OFFSET semantics would return wrong page. Fix: reject offset<0 with BadPaginationError like OffsetPaginator does.

findings.title: BasePaginator passes negative offset through for is_prev cursors
findings.body: File src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 182 computes start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. When cursor.is_prev is true a negative offset is passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. That preserves the old crash/incorrect behavior for prev cursors and contradicts the clamping done for forward cursors. A crafted prev cursor with negative offset causes AssertionError/500 or wrong results. Fix: clamp or validate offset >=0 for both directions.

findings.title: Direct dict access on end_timestamp_precise crashes consumer on missing field
findings.body: File src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py line 141 does val["end_timestamp_precise"] with no fallback. Any span event without that field raises KeyError inside process_batch, failing the whole batch, blocking commits and causing backlog/consumer crash-loop. The field was previously optional for tests and the schema may not guarantee it. Fix: use val.get with fallback to message timestamp/now and add validation.

findings.title: Removal of max_segment_spans guard hides silent eviction data loss
findings.body: File src/sentry/spans/buffer.py around line 449 removed the len(payloads)>max_segment_spans check that emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded and skipped oversize segments. The Lua script now silently ZPOPMINs everything over 1000 members. Oversize segments are therefore truncated with no metric/log, max_segment_spans config is dead, and downstream flush will emit incomplete segments while has_root_span/timeout logic still assumes full data. Fix: keep a metric/log for evicted spans and either enforce max_segment_spans or remove the option.

findings.title: Redirect depth cut from 10000 to 1000 breaks deep segments
findings.body: File src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua line 30 changed the redirect chase loop from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will stop resolving early, leaving set_span_id pointing at an intermediate set. Subsequent ZUNIONSTORE merges then split one logical segment across multiple keys, producing duplicate/incomplete flushed segments. There is no justification for the reduction; restore 10000 or make it configurable.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE without AGGREGATE corrupts scores on duplicates
findings.body: File src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua lines 47 and 53 call ZUNIONSTORE with default AGGREGATE SUM. Scores are end_timestamp_precise. If the same payload member exists in both source sets (retries, duplicate ingestion, overlapping merges) its score is doubled, corrupting ordering and causing the later ZPOPMIN eviction to keep/drop the wrong spans. Fix: pass AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) explicitly to preserve timestamp semantics.
